title: HumanBench save file, schema v1
description: DESIGN §8 (R-8.x) save file: sessions of raw responses, seen item and family ids, and an optional posterior cache. Strings are I-JSON (RFC 7493: no lone surrogates) so every valid file has an RFC 8785 canonical form. Signatures: the static MVP writes none, so its files are unverified; the per-session MAC of ROADMAP A16 (`sessions[].sig`, which names the anon_id it binds so it survives a merge) supersedes the file-level `sig` of the §8 example, which stays valid here. Notes settings: the optional `brief_prefs` (Phase AI, ROADMAP AI.7) holds the settings behind the "Notes for your AI" builder as enums, ids, versions, months and integers only, never free text; it was added to 1.0 before any save existed in the wild, so it needs no version bump. Versions: minor and patch bumps are additive within a major; a reader that cannot validate a file from a newer minor reports it as made by a newer version rather than dropping unknown fields. The TypeScript validator web/src/save/validate.ts mirrors this schema exactly and additionally rejects JSON nested deeper than 64 levels.

schema_version.description: Semver of this format. Major 1 is this schema; older majors are migrated (§8 merge step 5).

anon_id.description: 96 random bits in base62 behind an hb_ prefix (§8 privacy).

text.description: An I-JSON string: no unpaired UTF-16 surrogate (RFC 7493 §2.1, required by RFC 8785).

json.description: Any I-JSON value (response payloads and tuple extras are stored verbatim).

utc_seconds.description: UTC timestamp to the second, e.g. 2026-10-03T18:22:11Z (fixed width, so it sorts as text): a real Gregorian calendar time from 1970 (the session-id epoch) to 9999, so month lengths and leap years are part of the pattern (no 2026-02-30).

item_id.description: An item id, i:<fam>:<genver>:<seed> for procedural items (ROADMAP A11).

device.description: Coarse device class only (§8 privacy): no precise user agent.

family_name.description: A family such as macOS or Safari, never a version string (§8 privacy): no digits or dots.

flags.description: Integrity flag counters (§13); M1.19 adds more, so unknown snake_case flags are allowed. confidence_untouched_n counts the answers whose confidence slider was not moved (their confidence_pct is null). Session flags that are not counters: timed_tasks_only (true: the device half of an online sitting); continuation (true: the session continues the session just before it in time order, an interrupted session picked up again; the two are one sitting and share their test numbers in the §7.8 retest model; ignored on the first session); and how far the session got: done_<part> (true: the part ended normally in this session), completed (true: the session reached its end; finished_early and hard_stop are the other ends) and focus_session (true: a focus session).

response.description: [item_id, pretest (0/1), response, correct (0/1/null), rt_ms, confidence_pct, extra?] (§8). confidence_pct is null when no confidence was asked or the slider was not moved.

posterior_cache.description: A cache only (§7.8): readers re-score from responses and drop it when param_version differs or its shapes disagree.

brief_month.description: YYYY-MM, the only date the notes settings keep (no day-level timestamps).

brief_topic_id.description: A topic id of the controlled vocabulary (topics-v1), e.g. quant/probability_counting. Content labels only; the reader resolves it through the alias map.

brief_template_id.description: A line template id of the notes grammar, e.g. DS or U2.W3.

brief_line_key.description: A tick key or phrasing family root of the notes builder, e.g. FMT1 or U1.

brief_copied.description: What the person last copied or downloaded from the builder for one set of notes: the template release, the month, and each line's template id and wording version. It lets the app say, on a later visit, that a line was withdrawn or has new wording. No note text.

brief_context.description: One set of notes: where it is for and the person's own settings. Every string is an enum, an id or a version; interests, custom lines and names are never stored. `rev` rises with every edit; a merge keeps the copy with the higher rev per slot.

brief_context_removed.description: A set of notes the person removed. It keeps the slot and a rev above the removed set's, so a merge with an older copy of the save does not bring the set back.

brief_fit.description: One fit note: the person marked an explanation on a topic as too basic, about right or too much. Month only. It never enters scoring and is never uploaded.

brief_prefs.description: Notes settings (Phase AI, ROADMAP AI.7; proposal 5.5): sets of notes, fit notes and, in Part 2, the last suggested zones. Free text is never stored. They are removed before any upload (M2), never enter scoring, and merge by slot rev and by union of fit notes.

topics.description: Topic vocabulary version the ids were written under.

sig.description: Server HMAC over the file body (§8 example; superseded by ROADMAP A16). Only the server can verify it.

session_sig.description: ROADMAP A16 per-session server HMAC (M2.3) over the session without sig together with anon_id, the id it was issued to. A merge may change the file's anon_id, so the bound id travels with the sig. Only the server can verify it.
